kept.title: Unsafe Regex backtracking in HTML tag processing
kept.description: The `replaceTags` and `replaceBlocks` methods in `src/text-format.ts` use regex patterns that can cause catastrophic backtracking when processing malformed or crafted HTML with unclosed tags, leading to ReDoS (Regular Expression Denial of Service).
steps_to_exploit: Craft an HTML email with thousands of unclosed tags or specific patterns (e.g., <a href=).
Send the email to a system using `postal-mime` to parse it.
The CPU will spike to 100% and block the event loop, effectively crashing the parser or stalling the application.
kept.impact: Denial of Service (DoS) against any system relying on this library to parse emails.

kept.title: Lack of input sanitization in header processing
kept.description: `MimeNode.processHeaders` in `src/mime-node.ts` processes raw headers and passes them to `formatHtmlHeader` in `src/text-format.ts`. While there is some escaping, the parser is permissive with header keys and values, potentially allowing for XSS if the resulting parsed HTML is rendered in a browser.
steps_to_exploit: Craft an email header (e.g., Subject) containing malicious payload: ``.
Parse the email using `postal-mime`.
Render the output in an HTML view without additional context-aware sanitization.
kept.impact: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) in applications displaying parsed email content.

kept.title: Potential prototype pollution via `parseStructuredHeader`
kept.description: In `src/mime-node.ts`, `parseStructuredHeader` parses parameters into a plain object. If keys are not strictly validated, attackers could attempt to inject properties like `__proto__` or `constructor` into the `params` object.
steps_to_exploit: Craft a Content-Type header with a parameter name like `__proto__` or `prototype`.
Observe if the parser assigns this key to the object without checking.
Trigger logic that relies on `params` values to alter application state.
kept.impact: Arbitrary code execution or application logic corruption.

kept.title: Use of `TextDecoder` without proper validation for character sets
kept.description: `getDecoder` in `src/decode-strings.ts` falls back to `windows-1252` when an unknown charset is encountered. This may lead to encoding confusion or bypasses of security filters that rely on text inspection.
steps_to_exploit: Identify a security filter looking for specific strings (e.g., 'script').
Encode the script tags in a charset that the parser defaults to `windows-1252` or interprets differently.
Observe if the filter misses the payload while the parser executes it.
kept.impact: Bypassing security checks (WAF/Filters) via charset confusion.

kept.title: Insecure `npm update` script usage
kept.description: The `update` script in `package.json` performs `rm -rf node_modules package-lock.json && ncu -u && npm install` without verifying integrity or using a lockfile during the update process.
steps_to_exploit: A developer runs `npm run update`.
An attacker compromises a dependency version on the registry.
The script pulls the latest version without verifying hashes, leading to inclusion of malicious code.
kept.impact: Supply chain compromise via unverified dependency updates.

kept.title: Memory exhaustion via uncontrolled `ChunkWriter`
kept.description: The `ChunkWriter` class in `src/chunk-writer.ts` keeps an array of buffers. While it limits chunk sizes, a malicious email with extremely high numbers of small parts can still exhaust memory as `this.chunks` grows unbounded.
steps_to_exploit: Send an email with a massive number of small MIME attachments or parts.
The `ChunkWriter` collects these parts in the `chunks` array.
Memory usage continues to grow until the Node.js process crashes.
kept.impact: Denial of Service (DoS) via memory exhaustion.

kept.title: Path traversal risk in filename handling
kept.description: `collectAttachment` in `src/postal-mime.ts` extracts filenames from headers. These filenames are returned to the consumer, who may use them to write files to disk, potentially leading to path traversal.
steps_to_exploit: Craft an email with a Content-Disposition filename like `../../etc/passwd`.
Parse the email and write the attachment to the filesystem using the returned filename.
The file is written to an unintended directory.
kept.impact: Arbitrary file write on the system hosting the application.

kept.title: Weak logic in address extraction via regex
kept.description: The address parser in `src/address-parser.ts` attempts to recover addresses from malformed text using complex regex, which can be misled into picking up sensitive text or spoofing addresses.
steps_to_exploit: Craft a string that looks like a legitimate address to the `LOOSE_ADDR_SPEC` regex.
The parser extracts this string as a valid `from` or `to` address.
Use this for spoofing attacks or to trick the user into trusting the address.

kept.title: Missing enforcement of maximum nested groups in address parsing
kept.description: While `parseAddressList` in `src/address-parser.ts` uses `MAX_NESTED_GROUP_DEPTH`, a very deeply nested structure can trigger excessive recursion before hitting the limit.
steps_to_exploit: Craft an address string with extremely deep group nesting.
Trigger address parsing.
Stack exhaustion.
kept.impact: Application crash due to stack overflow.

kept.title: Potential for unbounded growth in `PassThroughDecoder`
kept.description: `PassThroughDecoder` in `src/pass-through-decoder.ts` manages chunks in an array. Similar to the `ChunkWriter`, it lacks strict total-size limits for the entire message body assembly.
steps_to_exploit: Send an email with a massive, non-encoded, non-multipart body.
The parser will accumulate the whole thing in memory before completion.

kept.title: Use of deprecated `Intl` locale handling
kept.description: `formatDate` in `src/text-format.ts` blindly uses `Intl.DateTimeFormat('default')`, which might behave unpredictably across different server environments.
steps_to_exploit: Change server locale.
Observe changes in date format which might cause parsing errors or logic gaps in downstream applications.
kept.impact: Inconsistent application state or logic errors.

kept.title: Potential DoS via large `maxHeadersSize` configuration
kept.description: The default `maxHeadersSize` of 2 MiB is quite generous for emails and can be configured even higher, allowing for potentially large amounts of memory to be locked per parsing instance.
steps_to_exploit: Configure `maxHeadersSize` to a high value.
Send many concurrent emails with headers just under the limit.
kept.impact: Increased risk of DoS under high concurrent load.

kept.title: Insufficient sanitization of `Content-Description` in `collectAttachment`
kept.description: `Content-Description` is decoded and included in the attachment object. If this is later used in an HTML context, it remains un-sanitized.
steps_to_exploit: Set `Content-Description` to `<script>alert(1)</script>`.
Access the `description` field in the resulting attachment object.
Render in HTML.

kept.title: Loose parsing of header values allowing malformed headers
kept.description: `MimeNode.processHeaders` attempts to be robust, but it might misinterpret headers used for security-critical decisions by downstream components.
steps_to_exploit: Supply multiple headers of the same key with different values.
Observe if the parser selects a different one than a proxy or mail filter.
kept.impact: Bypassing security policies or logic mismatch.

kept.title: Potential for OOM on `decodeURIComponentWithCharset` with large strings
kept.description: The function `decodeURIComponentWithCharset` processes strings that could be very large, resulting in large temporary `ArrayBuffer` allocations.
steps_to_exploit: Send a header containing a very long percent-encoded string.
The parser allocates a large `ArrayBuffer` and `encodedBytes` array.
